html:
To re-register for VAT, you apply to HMRC in the same way as a brand-new business: online through HMRC's register for VAT service, or by post on form VAT1 in a few special cases. You must do it if your taxable turnover goes back over the £90,000 VAT threshold, and you can choose to do it earlier. If you use FreeAgent, you can carry on in the same account by adding a new VAT registration period.

When do you have to re-register for VAT?

The rules are the same as for any business. The VAT registration threshold is £90,000 of taxable turnover, and the Autumn Budget on 28 October 2026 left it unchanged. You must register if you meet either of two tests.

The look-back test

At the end of every month, add up your taxable turnover for the last 12 months. If it's gone over £90,000, you must register within 30 days of the end of that month. You're registered from the first day of the second month after you went over. So if you go over in May, you register by 30 June and you're VAT-registered from 1 July.

The look-forward test

If you expect your taxable turnover in the next 30 days alone to go over £90,000, say because you've just signed a big contract, you must register by the end of those 30 days. Your registration starts from the date you realised.

Taxable turnover is everything you sell that isn't exempt from VAT, including zero-rated sales. Sales you made while you were registered last time don't usually count.

Can you re-register voluntarily?

Yes, even if your turnover is below £90,000. You can then reclaim VAT on your business costs, and if your clients are VAT-registered businesses they can usually reclaim the VAT you charge, so it often costs them nothing. If you mostly sell to the public, adding 20% to your prices makes you more expensive, so weigh that up first.

How to re-register for VAT with HMRC

  1. Apply online. You can usually register online, and you can save your answers and come back later. Have your turnover figures and the date you went over the threshold to hand.
  2. Use form VAT1 if you have to. A few cases must go by post. The one most relevant when re-registering is asking for an exception because your turnover has only gone over the threshold temporarily.
  3. Wait for your VAT number. HMRC sends a 9-digit VAT registration number by post. It must go on every invoice you raise.
  4. Don't show VAT until it arrives. You can raise your prices to cover the VAT you'll owe, then reissue the invoices showing VAT once your number comes through.

An accountant can also send your VAT returns and deal with HMRC for you. See gov.uk's how to register for VAT page for the full list.

What happens to your old VAT number?

HMRC can sometimes reinstate a cancelled registration with your agreement, as if you'd never deregistered. Its standard practice is to allow this within six months of the cancellation date. Otherwise, you're registered again under the normal rules with a new VAT number [CONFIRM: HMRC issues a new number on re-registration; its manual covers reinstating the old one, not reuse]. Don't put your old number on invoices.

Making Tax Digital for VAT

When you register, HMRC signs your business up to Making Tax Digital for VAT unless you're exempt. You keep digital records and send returns through compatible software, such as FreeAgent. Returns are usually every 3 months, and the deadline to file and pay is usually one calendar month and 7 days after each period ends. Our Making Tax Digital guide has more.

VAT schemes worth considering

Flat Rate Scheme

You pay HMRC a fixed percentage of your VAT-inclusive turnover instead of working out VAT on every sale and purchase. You can join if your VAT turnover is £150,000 or less (excluding VAT). You must leave if your turnover for the last 12 months was over £230,000 (including VAT) on the anniversary of joining, or you expect it to go over that in the next 30 days alone.

If you mostly sell your time, check this carefully. If you spend less than 2% of your turnover on goods, or less than £1,000 a year, you're a limited cost business and pay 16.5%, which wipes out the benefit for many contractors. There's a 1% discount in your first year as a VAT-registered business [CONFIRM: whether the 1% first-year discount applies when you re-register].

Cash Accounting Scheme

You pay VAT on sales when your customers pay you, and reclaim it on purchases when you've paid your suppliers. That helps if clients pay slowly. You can join if your estimated VAT taxable turnover for the next 12 months is £1.35 million or less, and must leave above £1.6 million. You can't combine it with the Flat Rate Scheme.

Setting FreeAgent up again

You don't need a new copy of FreeAgent. You add a new VAT registration period to your existing account. Before you start, your previous period must be marked as de-registered with a date, its final VAT return must be filed or marked as filed, and you need full (level 8) access [CONFIRM: FreeAgent re-registration steps and access level still current]. Then:

  1. Change your VAT registration status.
  2. Enter your new VAT settings.
  3. Enter your new VAT registration details, including your VAT number and registration date.
  4. Enter your new VAT return details.

FreeAgent then prepares returns for the new period under Taxes, then VAT. Old periods stay in Settings, under VAT Registration. Once the new period exists, changes to transactions in the old period won't flow into your new returns. FreeAgent's re-registration guide shows each screen. As a FreeAgent Gold Partner, we can check your settings, and a FreeAgent subscription is included in all our plans.

Penalties for registering late

Register late and you'll owe HMRC the VAT on your sales from the date you should have registered, even if you never charged it. HMRC can also charge a failure to notify penalty, worked out as a percentage of that VAT:

  • not deliberate, and you tell HMRC yourself within 12 months: 0% to 30%
  • not deliberate, but later or only after HMRC prompts you: a minimum of 10% or 20%
  • deliberate: up to 70%, or up to 100% if it was concealed

There's no penalty if you had a reasonable excuse, it wasn't deliberate and you told HMRC without unreasonable delay. HMRC's failure to notify factsheet has the detail.

Questions people ask

How long do I have to re-register for VAT?

30 days from the end of the month your rolling 12-month turnover went over £90,000. If you expect to go over in the next 30 days alone, register by the end of those 30 days.

Will I get my old VAT number back?

Only if HMRC agrees to reinstate your old registration, which it normally allows within six months of cancellation.

Can I keep using the same FreeAgent account?

Yes. Close off the old period, file its final return, then add a new VAT registration period.

Do I have to re-register if I'm under £90,000?

No, but you can choose to. It often makes sense if your clients are VAT-registered.
